`gov dispatch tick` does one pass

a planted project: two `tick` calls started together run one pass (the second exits at the lock, writing nothing); a planted OFF file makes `tick` exit without starting anything; the host's cron or service entry runs it every minute and after a restart (read from the installed entry, no agent session in its chain); `gov dispatch status` prints the status.
It starts at most one session per pass

planted ready lists with several entries: one session starts per pass, staggered; an entry not on the orchestrator's list is never started; entries with an uncommitted claim, an unclean worktree, an incomplete brief, a running ticket, an unread return, a shut gate or a full disk are each skipped and named with their reason.
Peaks, not the moment

planted job histories for each kind of job: the status prints each kind's peak (CPU and memory) with its date, refreshed from the history within a day; a start is refused when the room is under the new peak plus the peaks ahead and made when it is over; the memory floor and working size read are the gate's.
Every heavy step takes a heavy-job slot
a planted heavy step (test run, rebuild, full check, retrieval measure) is shown holding a slot; a planted one running with no slot is named in the status as a finding.
Every finished session's return becomes one inbox item

a planted finished session: one inbox item, and none more on the next pass; a planted start that never ran: one inbox item; a planted item unread past the configured time: one escalation pushed by the notifier stub to the orchestrator's owner.
Every ticket the orchestrator approved to land

planted approvals: an approved ticket goes to the landing command as one batch when the tree is clean, on the integration branch and no close runs; an unapproved ticket never goes; an approved one never goes twice (the approval is claimed before the launch); each outcome is an inbox item.
A status file every pass

after a planted pass the status file holds the running sessions (counted from processes by the launcher's identity marker), load, memory, gate, slots held, peaks ahead, queue and inbox; after a planted failing pass the top line says the pass failed and the file is not a stale one that looks current.
Nothing project-specific in the code

grep of the dispatcher code for this repository's branches, paths and ticket ids finds 0 lines; planted tests exist and fail for each named refusal (uncommitted claim, shut gate, no room for a peak, running ticket, unread return, malformed list line, hung command, crash after a launch); the independent review's record exists before the dispatcher is switched on; this repository's tool is no longer the one running.
A landing never waits for a close

planted closes: a running close with a ticket in the landing's set blocks the landing, as does one committing its records; a running close with no shared ticket does not block it; two record commits at the same time both land (one retried).
Nothing holds the machine unseen

a planted hung embedding server (the fixed request unanswered past the configured time) and a planted idle slot holder (its process tree's CPU time flat past the configured time): each gives one inbox item and one alert on the notifier stub, once per incident, cleared on recovery; the server restarts only through the configured safe restart, rate-limited and recorded; the holder's process is still running afterwards.
The dispatcher never starts a third review round
a planted ticket with two probe records: its next review launch is not started and the ticket becomes one owner item in the inbox; a planted ticket with one probe record is started.
No watcher needs re-arming
a planted run across a restart: every wake the caller gets is an inbox item written by a pass, and no watcher process or re-arm step is present or needed.
While ready work waits, busy cores stay

planted history of hours with ready work waiting: the daily report gives the share of hours with busy cores inside the configured band (at least 80 % passes, below it is flagged) and lists the time below and above the band with its cause.
The project's nightly is never kept from starting

a planted configured hold time before the nightly: from then until its running marker (or the latest time) no landing is claimed, a landing already running is finalised, and the status names the hold.
Each pass reads the GPU state

planted server logs: a crash line, and a model loaded with 0 layers on a GPU it is expected to use, each give one inbox item at once and one sentinel line, once per incident; a healthy log gives none; the status shows the GPU, its holders and each model's layers.
`gov watch` wakes its caller

a planted lead worktree gains a commit marking a key result (probe record, measure, package, baseline) and a lead returns: `gov watch` wakes its caller once for each, named; with a dispatcher running, `gov watch` only reads the inbox and the return is not marked seen.
A commit brought into a lead's branch by a merge
a planted lead branch merged from the integration branch: `gov watch` does not wake its caller for the merged-in commit.
Every commit id and path a return names
planted returns naming a real commit and path and a nonexistent one: the inbox item for the second names the one that does not resolve; the first names none.
gov launch lead <ticket> builds the whole lead

`gov launch lead <ticket>` on a planted ticket prints or writes an invocation holding absolute paths, the identity in --settings, the model, background mode, and the log and PID files, and the resource gate's check ran before it started (a planted shut gate refuses).
The ready list the dispatcher reads
a planted list from `gov plan --ready` committed by the orchestrator: the dispatcher starts only entries on it and in no order of its own; an entry not on it is not started.
A session started for an entry not on the ready list

planted passes with an off-list entry, a not-ready one, a running one and one with no room for its peak: no session starts for any; an unapproved ticket and an approved one a second time are not landed; a finished return missing from the inbox, and a lead count taken from anything but processes, are each absent.
A key result or a return reported twice
a planted key-result commit and a planted return, each present through several passes: each is reported once, and each planted one is reported (none missing).
